thread.title: Stay Long Apple, Avoid IBM and J&J: Strategas | Investopedia

author: Shoshanna Delventhal
title: Stay Long Apple, Avoid IBM and J&J: Strategas | Investopedia
text:
Stay Long Apple, Avoid IBM and J&J: Strategas By Shoshanna Delventhal | May 7, 2018 — 1:29 PM EDT
While the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) spiked late last week, jumping some 300 points on Friday, roughly two thirds of the 30 companies that make up the blue-chip index were trading in correction territory or worse, as outlined by CNBC . One technician has isolated two Dow stocks he sees as likely to drag on the index, as well as one set to outperform over the long term.
Chris Verrone, head of technical analysis at Strategas Research Partners, spoke in an interview with CNBC on Thursday, recommending that investors avoid shares of Johnson & Johnson ( JNJ ) and International Business Machines Corp. ( IBM ) and go long on Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) stock.
IBM stock suffered its worst day in four years last month on full-year guidance , which fell short of the Street's expectations. Despite beating the consensus estimates for top line and bottom line numbers, investors have become impatient with the company's turnaround plan and discouraged by slowing growth in IBM's new strategic imperatives segment. Last week, ahead of Berkshire Hathaway Inc.'s ( BRK.A ) annual shareholder meeting , CEO Warren Buffett told CNBC that the Omaha-based conglomerate had sold off the remainder of its stake in the old-guard IT provider. Multiyear Uptrends for Legacy IT Giant Are Over
Strategas said that IBM "is in the midst of this multiyear top breaking down late last year and then rolling over here again." Veronne pegged $140 as the stock's key support . "We don't think it holds. We think ultimately that one is headed lower." Trading down 0.2% on Monday morning at $143.54, IBM reflects 6.5% decline year-to-date (YTD) and a 7.4% fall over 12 months, underperforming the broader S&P 500 's 0.2% gain and 11.6% return over the same respective periods. This story is based off a Friday CNBC report. (See also: Berkshire Hathaway Has Exited IBM: Buffett. )
As for J&J, Veronne outlines a similarly downbeat forecast. Pointing to the stock's chart, the analyst stated that the "multiyear uptrend is now broken," leaving JNJ as one of the "more broken, vulnerable names," out there. In March, JNJ's 200-day moving average moved above its 50-day moving average, a technical indicator typically signaling a bearish trend. JNJ stock, trading at $124.38, has sank nearly 11% YTD and is up 0.7% over 12 months. Apple to Surge Another 10% Above New High
Verrone expects AAPL stock to gain nearly 9% from Friday close to reach $200 in 12 months. AAPL opened at a new all-time high on Monday on news that Warren Buffett had upped his stake in the company to 5%. The famed investor followed up with with comments suggesting that he would buy the entire company if he could. Trading up about 1% on Monday morning at $185.74, AAPL reflects a 9.8% gain YTD and a 24.7% increase over 12 months. (See also: Apple iPhone X: World's Best-Selling Phone in Q1. )
